name: Kutná Hora
tagline: A once-fabulously wealthy medieval silver-mining town, its skyline still ruled by a soaring Gothic cathedral and its most famous chapel decorated entirely in human bone.
highlight: Stepping into the Sedlec Ossuary and realising the chandeliers, garlands and coat of arms overhead are all built from real human bones.
shortDescription: A once-fabulously wealthy medieval silver-mining town near Prague, home to the Sedlec Ossuary's bone-decorated chapel and the soaring Gothic St Barbara's Cathedral.

intro: Kutná Hora is genuinely one of Bohemia's most rewarding day trips from Prague, a once-fabulously wealthy medieval town built on one of Europe's richest silver deposits.
That wealth genuinely built an extraordinary Gothic cathedral rivalling Prague's own, alongside a royal mint that once produced coinage used across Central Europe.

Its most famous sight is genuinely far stranger — the Sedlec Ossuary, a small chapel decorated entirely with the bones of tens of thousands of people, arranged into chandeliers, garlands and a coat of arms.

whyVisit.intro: Kutná Hora's case rests genuinely on extraordinary Gothic architecture paired with one of Europe's strangest, most memorable sights.

points.title: The Sedlec Ossuary is genuinely unlike anywhere else
points.text: A small chapel decorated entirely in human bone, arranged with genuine artistry rather than morbid excess.

points.title: St Barbara's Cathedral genuinely rivals Prague's own Gothic churches
points.text: Flying buttresses and soaring vaults built on the wealth of the town's silver mines.

points.title: It's genuinely an easy, well-connected day trip
points.text: A direct train from Prague takes under an hour.

points.title: The history here is genuinely fascinating
points.text: A medieval boomtown whose silver once funded much of the Bohemian kingdom.

points.title: It's genuinely far quieter than Prague itself
points.text: A real, lived-in Czech town rather than a purely tourist-facing centre.

attractionsIntro: Kutná Hora's essential sights are genuinely spread between Sedlec's ossuary and the historic centre's Gothic core.

attractions.name: Sedlec Ossuary

image.file: File:Sedlec Ossuary Bone Church Kutna Hora (35022287782).jpg
image.alt: The bone-decorated interior of the Sedlec Ossuary

attractions.text: Genuinely the town's most famous and startling sight, a small chapel decorated with the bones of an estimated 40,000 to 70,000 people.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book a timed-entry ticket online ahead — this small chapel gets genuinely busy with day-trippers.

attractions.name: St Barbara's Cathedral

image.alt: St Barbara's Cathedral in Kutná Hora

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Bohemia's most spectacular Gothic cathedrals, built by the town's silver miners' guild and dedicated to their patron saint.
attractions.tip: Genuinely look up at the ribbed vaulting — it's considered one of the finest examples of late Gothic architecture anywhere.

attractions.name: The Italian Court (Vlašský dvůr)

image.alt: The courtyard of the Italian Court in Kutná Hora

attractions.text: Genuinely the former royal mint and palace, where medieval Bohemia's silver groschen coins were struck.
attractions.tip: Genuinely tour the interior to see the original minting workshop and royal chapel.

attractions.name: Church of St James

image.file: File:Kutná Hora - Šultysova - View SSE towards Church of St. James (Kostel sv. Jakuba).jpg
image.alt: The Church of St James in Kutná Hora

attractions.text: Genuinely the town's tallest landmark, its single Gothic tower visible from across the historic centre.
attractions.tip: Genuinely pair a visit with the neighbouring Italian Court, just steps away.

attractions.name: The Stone Fountain

image.alt: The late-Gothic Stone Fountain in Kutná Hora

attractions.text: Genuinely a beautifully carved late-Gothic water reservoir, once part of the town's medieval water supply.
attractions.tip: Genuinely easy to combine with a wander through the surrounding old town streets.

attractions.name: The Hrádek Silver Mine Museum

image.file: File:Kutná Hora - Barborská - View South on Silvermine Museum Hrádek.jpg
image.alt: The Hrádek Silver Mine Museum in Kutná Hora

attractions.text: Genuinely the place to understand the wealth behind the town, with tours descending into a genuine medieval mine shaft.
attractions.tip: Genuinely wear warm layers — the underground tour is noticeably cooler than the surface.

attractions.name: Kutná Hora's historic streets

image.alt: A historic street in Kutná Hora's old town

attractions.text: Genuinely worth simply wandering, a compact UNESCO-listed old town of Gothic and baroque facades with far fewer crowds than Prague.
attractions.tip: Genuinely allow time to wander without a fixed plan between the main sights.

thingsToDoIntro: Kutná Hora genuinely rewards a full day, split between Sedlec's ossuary and the historic centre proper.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Sedlec Ossuary

image.file: File:Sedlec Ossuary Bone Church Kutna Hora (35056879451).jpg
image.alt: Bone decorations inside the Sedlec Ossuary

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential, slightly eerie highlight, the small chapel's bone chandelier the most photographed detail.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely visit first thing, as it's a short bus or taxi ride from the main town centre.

thingsToDo.title: Tour St Barbara's Cathedral

image.alt: The interior of St Barbara's Cathedral in Kutná Hora

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential stop, taking in the cathedral's soaring nave and medieval mining-themed frescoes.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely walk the terrace outside for a view back over the Vrchlice valley.

thingsToDo.title: Walk through the Italian Court

image.alt: The Italian Court's courtyard and buildings in Kutná Hora

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile stop, touring the former royal mint where Bohemia's medieval silver coinage was struck.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with the Church of St James next door in the same visit.

thingsToDo.title: Descend into a medieval silver mine

image.file: File:Kutná Hora - Barborská - Gate to Garden Hrádek Silvermine Museum.jpg
image.alt: The entrance to the Hrádek Silver Mine Museum

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fascinating underground tour, descending into the shaft that built the town's medieval fortune.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead in peak season — tour group sizes are limited underground.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the Stone Fountain

image.alt: The carved Gothic Stone Fountain in Kutná Hora

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quick, worthwhile stop, one of the finest surviving pieces of Gothic civic architecture in the country.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely easy to fit in while walking between the main square and St James's church.

thingsToDo.title: Wander the UNESCO-listed old town

image.alt: Streets in Kutná Hora's historic old town

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an hour or two, with far fewer crowds than Prague's equivalent streets.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely stop for lunch at a local restaurant well away from the ossuary's tour-bus car park.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Kutná Hora day trip noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely a timed-entry Sedlec Ossuary ticket online ahead in peak season.
Take genuinely the train over an organised tour if you'd like more flexibility on timing.
Wear genuinely comfortable shoes — the historic centre is built on a hill with plenty of cobblestones.
Pack genuinely a light layer for the underground silver mine tour, which runs noticeably cooler.
Eat genuinely lunch away from the streets nearest the ossuary for better value.
Combine genuinely Sedlec and the historic centre in one visit — they're an easy bus ride apart.

faq.q: Is Kutná Hora worth a day trip from Prague?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the Sedlec Ossuary and St Barbara's Cathedral are both extraordinary, and the direct train makes it an easy half-day or full-day trip.

faq.q: How do you get from Prague to Kutná Hora?
faq.a: Genuinely easiest by direct train, taking under an hour from Prague's main station.

faq.q: Is the Sedlec Ossuary respectful to visit?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely, treated as a place of quiet reflection — visitors are asked to stay respectful and photography rules are enforced.

faq.q: How much time do you need in Kutná Hora?
faq.a: A full day genuinely covers both the ossuary and the historic centre comfortably; a rushed half-day covers the essentials.

faq.q: Can you combine Kutná Hora with another day trip?
faq.a: It's genuinely possible but rushed — most visitors find one destination per day trip from Prague works better.
The Sedlec Ossuary genuinely gets busy with tour groups by mid-morning; the historic centre itself stays noticeably quieter.
